title: Nakshi kantha embroidery
summary: Nakshi kantha is the stitched quilt of Bengal: women layer worn cotton cloth and cover it with fine rows of running stitch, drawing lotus medallions, trees, fish, birds and paddy borders in coloured thread that once came from the cloth's own edges.
howToPlay: Choose a thread colour and a motif from the basket.
Touch a square to stitch it; the matching square on the other side of the quilt is stitched too.
Follow the pencil chart, then press Check to compare your quilt with the pattern.
rules: The quilt is a mirror image from left to right, as most quilt layouts are.
A square counts only when its motif and its thread colour both match the pattern.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Nakshi kantha is made in Bangladesh and in West Bengal, where rural households have long turned old saris and lungis into quilts, and often a single piece takes months. Mymensingh, Jessore, Rajshahi and Faridpur are known for their own styles.
